text: Could we enhance citizen autonomy and interactions with the Government by digitalising some of the functions or decisions we take in the community?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Our Government probably has an application for anything somewhere.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But it would perhaps make better sense to consolidate and streamline so that citizens are clear about where to go for what.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Or simply, just go to one platform for everything they need.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In the course of our constituency work, we would have observed that, within the community, there are many ideas and resources.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: For example, we have multiple voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and informal volunteer groups, all of which have lion-hearted volunteers who want to do more for our people.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In MacPherson, the creation of the MacPherson Cares app is an example.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Amongst the many things we hope to achieve, we wanted to draw the volunteers into a central pool and seniors can tap on them for requests as simple as helping them to read letters.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In our drive towards a Smart Nation, the Government's effort alone is not enough.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, I would like to ask how can the Government better partner citizens in the co-creation of Smart Nation?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung could answer your points.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When COVID-19 broke upon us, you may have noticed that apps like MaskGoWhere or even the gov.sg Whatsapp channel were up and running almost overnight, literally within days.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think Members all know that this is only possible because, over the last couple of years, we have assiduously built up the talent and capability.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And this is one clear and present example where it has enabled us to do things quickly in an agile way and in a way that matters for real life.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I want to assure Mr Cedric Foo that we are exquisitely conscious that Smart Nation has to benefit citizens in tangible ways.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have reorganised our services around the needs of citizens, we have made it easier and faster for citizens to access all Government services.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: A prime example I would cite is the Moments of Life (MOL) app.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When this app first started, we were aiming to enable parents to quickly register their child’s birth and apply for the Baby Bonus that Minister Josephine Teo was providing and to reduce the time that parents needed to apply for this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think Minister Josephine Teo will appreciate that it is much easier to improve productivity in apps than it is the TFR.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In September 2019, MOL was expanded to serve the needs of our seniors as well, and MOH will elaborate on this in its COS debate.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As we expand the suite of services we provide through MOL, we will continue to improve the app through constant user testing and citizen engagement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Smart Nation has to be about solving problems innovatively in both simple and complex issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We introduced the concept of a digital medical certificate (MC) in 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If Members think about it, it should be easier to submit and to keep records for digital MCs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We first tested this at the National Heart Centre.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The GovTech team worked with the healthcare practitioners in the Heart Centre to improve the pilot solution, before rolling it out to more places.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will be expanding this to other hospitals and clinics, in particular, into the private sector, starting with Raffles Medical and Mount Alvernia Hospital.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I agree with Mr Teo Ser Luck and Mr Ong Teng Koon that building a Smart Nation should also help businesses to succeed in this digital era.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Over the past few years, we made it easier for businesses to transact digitally with the Government through the various initiatives like the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) Go app and Business Grants Portal.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are extending our support for businesses to help them through their different phases, from starting up a business, to seizing opportunities to grow, to running it more efficiently on a day-to-day basis.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To give you an example, we launched the GoBusiness Licensing portal in October 2019, using the customer journey approach, to help food and beverage (F&B) businesses start.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Some Members may know that, in fact, applying for the right licence to start a business – and, in particular, the F&B business – can be an extremely onerous process, with 14 different licences and 800-over fields to fill.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When we launched the portal for the F&B processes, we were able to simplify not only the application process but, more importantly, the backend re-engineering that would save time and, ultimately, increase the opportunities for them to get online and to conduct their business instantly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I agree with Mr Lim Swee Say and Mr Teo Ser Luck that AI should be one of Singapore’s key strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you think about the transition from having computing power in the 1980s to connectivity in the 1990s, today, the fact that computer systems can now engage in pattern recognition, whether it is facial recognition, speech or hearing, this is transformative.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I want to emphasise the word here is "deployment" because we will never have the oceans of data that China has, or the depth and unique ecosystem that Silicon Valley has.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I think we have a niche when it comes to deployment, especially in areas where we already have a competitive advantage, for instance, in healthcare, education, logistics, Smart City, Urban Solutions and security.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are also putting in place ecosystem enablers to facilitate this AI deployment across the board.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This includes making it easier for companies to adopt AI solutions and we have programmes like SMEsGoDigital and AI Singapore’s 100 Experiments programme and these are available to the private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to take a human-centric approach to AI to bring tangible benefits to citizens and businesses – I am trying to address Mr Pritam Singh's point here – whilst putting in place a strong AI governance structure to ensure that these new fangled abilities are used responsibly, the risks are managed appropriately and public trust is maintained.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To ensure benefits to citizens and businesses are widespread and sustained, we have also invested heavily in digital infrastructure at the national level.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There is a lot of behind-the-scenes work, often unnoticed and under-appreciated.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But, like physical infrastructure, these are fundamental to our ongoing digital transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The National Digital Identity (NDI) – this is one piece of digital infrastructure that most people would probably not have heard of.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But Members would have heard of SingPass Mobile.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It has enabled us to make it easy and secure to verify identity and I am sure many Members of this House have used SingPass for a variety of log-ons in order to use Government services.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mind you, in the past, it would require you to go down to the branch with your witnesses and beneficiaries, sign in front of someone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Now, with the NDI system and Government systems online, you can do all these entirely online but securely because of the NDI system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Businesses have also used this NDI system to innovate and to raise the quality of their own digital services which are provided to customers at large.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For instance, online retailers like Carousell which have promoted users as verified buyers or sellers when they sign up using MyInfo, thereby building up trust in online transactions and the marketplace.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I should have explained MyInfo is basically linked to the NDI so that people do not have to repeatedly fill forms.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As long as I have verified that online user, a carefully curated set of information which the user authorises is then made available to that business.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Apart from digital identity, we have also made significant improvements in digital payment infrastructure to support more use cases and to make sure it remains interoperable and competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Monthly transaction volumes nearly doubled over the course of last year, from 4.2 million to 8.1 million transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are using PayNow more pervasively in our Government services and we are seeing high take-up rates.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Through these efforts, citizens' and businesses' satisfaction rates have gone up.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members know that we conduct regular surveys on this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We discovered that there has been an eight percentage point increase from 2018 to 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Currently, those who are indicating satisfaction with Government digital services have gone up to about 86% and 77% respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These are the highest scores since we started measuring them in 2012.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I say this not to blow our trumpets but to tell people that we are focused on the citizens' experience and on making sure we deliver real value to citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to improve digital services for both citizens and businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the last count, we have about 100 Government apps.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I do not take joy in that number, because citizens often tell me, "There are so many.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Which one do I use?" To remedy this, we will systematically streamline the number of apps and our digital offerings.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For a start, we will improve and reorganise the MOL app, which I described just now, with the eventual aim of personalising it for each user, as Ms Tin Pei Ling had suggested.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If Members think about it, we may all carry smartphones, but everybody's home screen is unique.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And in a sense, the question is not the number of apps but whether those apps are customised and are suitable for you.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Citizens will soon be able to access common Government services on MOL, like managing taxes and CPF matters, or even to make event bookings.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These processes will continue to be reviewed and, as I said, do not pay attention to the number of apps, pay attention to whether it meets your needs and, more importantly, whether at the backend, the Government is using this as an opportunity to re-engineer our processes to be more efficient, to be more cost-effective and to be more responsive.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For businesses, we will be extending the user-centric approach that we have taken in setting up the GoBusiness Licensing portal to help more businesses meet their different needs as they start up, as they grow and as they run.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will streamline our digital transactions, make them even more user-centric, and provide businesses with information and tools so that they can capitalise on opportunities and to reduce cost.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) will elaborate on this during its COS debate.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will also be exploring more NDI use cases for businesses in order to make it cheaper, easier and faster for them to go digital.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are testing the use of SingPass by businesses so that they do not have to build and secure their own digital identity verification systems.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Union members can currently access the U Portal via SingPass and Republic Plaza grants building access when visitors enter via SingPass Mobile.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: No more surrendering your National Registration Identity Card.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also ran a 12-month pilot last year for MyInfo Business to help SMEs prefill their Government-verified data for bank account opening and loan applications.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Later this year, we will extend such prefilling to more business-to-business (B2B) services.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Of course, a Smart Nation must go beyond just fancy online services and apps.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It must improve the daily lived experience, as emphasised by Dr Teo Ho Pin.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Pritam Singh has asked about the trials of Lamppost as a Platform in one-north and Geylang, and I thank him for asking that.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They have the advantage of being in a fixed location.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These attributes have made them very convenient to deploy sensors on.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are deploying sensors and testing out some use cases.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For instance, to keep track of environmental quality sensing, traffic congestion and crowd safety.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think that the key point that the Member made is balance: that we must get the balance right between acquiring data, using it and protecting privacy and security.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It will be identifiable only when absolutely necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For instance, in service delivery or in the case of facial recognition, if the Police need it to identify missing persons or for the purposes of investigation, then, under carefully controlled circumstances, that will be enabled.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There is increased capacity to deal with rapidly changing circumstances and emergencies in the real world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to evolve how the Government operates innovatively in a digital environment and we will work even more closely in partnership with our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, to support our fight against COVID-19, many GovTech engineers worked with the rest of the Public Service to build new digital services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This was identified as an urgent need to allay fears, provide accurate, reliable and real-time information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Other teams worked on providing accurate information through the Gov.sg WhatsApp channel, Ask Jamie chatbot and developing software to help the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) monitor Leave of Absence compliance – just to name a few of these digital efforts to support our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I recently met Mr Ryan Tan, who was part of the team that put together MaskGoWhere.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He has been with GovTech for five years, having joined us through the Technology Associate Programme immediately upon his graduation from NUS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The team started with three people, scaled up to 30 people over a weekend and then, back down to three or four when it became stable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He applied his skills in cloud architecture and app development and deployment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He also applied the analytics tools that he works on in his normal job, embedding them within MaskGoWhere so that the team was able to optimise their service's response in real time, as it received almost a million unique views over a very short time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This story of Ryan and other members of the MaskGoWhere team is an example of how we are transforming digital Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Their willingness to step forward and rapidly put together what they understood was a solution to an urgent problem and the fact that they had the tools and capabilities to do so immediately demonstrates that we are well on the way to becoming a Government that is "digital to the core" and "serving with a heart".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These outcomes are only possible because we decided to build up the digital engineering capability of the Government into a strategic capability a few years ago.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With this strong engineering core, we can internalise within our service the capabilities and the skills, to use technology to transform our core businesses as well as develop the confidence to integrate with external stakeholders and the private sector, building platforms, such as MyInfo, not just for ourselves but to enable our whole economy to innovate and digitalise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, to Mr Vikram Nair's question, we will continue to invest in engineering capabilities, create the right environment and exciting opportunities for engineers to apply their ingenuity to serve the public good.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: More than developing good people, we have had to re-engineer how we use technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As Prof Lim Sun Sun has mentioned, more data will also be shared with companies and researchers in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The progress that we have made in allowing this type of data sharing and the use of cloud-based services were also key factors that have enabled the MaskGoWhere team to deliver their swift and effective response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree with the suggestions made by Mr Darryl David and Dr Yaacob Ibrahim on the importance of maintaining public trust in our use of data and I would like to assure Members that the implementation of the Public Sector Data Security Review Committee (PSDSRC) is on track.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also migrated non-sensitive IT systems to the cloud to take advantage of the latest technology and to improve cost-effectiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Similarly, we are adopting the best practices in software development by building a technology stack with modular software components for reuse and sharing across agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Putting all these together, we can more effectively harness digitalisation to serve our citizens and businesses better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Despite the Coronavirus Disease of 2019 (COVID-19), work continues on many platforms, products and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Moments of Life (MOL) is one example and GoBusiness is another which embody how we use digital technology to integrate services across agencies to be more user-centric.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Public Service Division (PSD) will give further elaboration on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But we must also create new value for citizens to be "digital to the core".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This portal uses machine learning, matching jobseekers to relevant opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Its job recommendations are personalised to the preferences and skills of each jobseeker, and it will get better and improve its performance over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We hope that, with this approach, we can also design better policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This has started and a team from the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has used a cross-agency administrative dataset to review how Workfare can strengthen retirement adequacy of lower-income workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Their analysis informed the Workfare enhancements that were announced in the last Budget and implemented since the start of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To best serve the needs of our society and citizens, we need to actively partner Singaporeans in building our Smart Nation, a point made by Ms Tin Pei Ling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ours is a digital version of SG Together comprising two broad strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We hope to demystify technology and to encourage as many citizens as possible to visit these exhibits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For the second collaborative design strategy, we have previously launched with an initiative called Smart Nation Co-creating with Our People Everywhere (SCOPE), where citizens try out early prototypes of our products and share their thoughts on how they can be refined.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It has allowed us to continually test our ideas and improve them over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example, when we were developing the Active Ageing features for MOL, many seniors suggested that the app should help them find exercise events nearby.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This was not something that we had prioritised, but we adjusted our plans and now this is one of the most popular features of that service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Second, we will bring SCOPE closer to residents by holding the sessions on board a Smart Nation Builder mobile truck, which will slowly make its way around Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Please look out for it when it comes to your neighbourhood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to make sure that we build digital readiness in Singaporeans so that they can take advantage of these opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) will share more on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, our swift response to the COVID-19 situation is a glimpse of how Smart Nation is already here to impact our daily lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We must continue to transform how Government works by re-engineering our digital resources, investing in our people and co-creating with the public.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Scamming is not only lucrative, it is also getting more sophisticated.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Some scams do not put it on the nature of greed.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: They are disguised as service calls from telecommunications companies (telcos), banks or Government authorities.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: These scams capitalise on the victims' lack of knowledge on how things function in the Internet age.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: An innocuous call is all it takes for the scammer to try to gain remote access to the victim's computer, bank account information, personal identification number and one-time password.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: It is very painful and sad to read in the news about elderly Singaporeans being scammed in this manner time and again, despite all the efforts by the Police to educate the public about such crimes.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: In the pursuit of a cashless society and a Smart Nation, have we made life a breeze for one generation and more vulnerable for another?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I am for progress, but I am deeply concerned that some Singaporeans would be exposed to untold dangers in the digital jungle.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Most of the scams leverage one thing in common to make a clean getaway – the speed of online banking transactions.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: By the time a Police report is made, the victims' money would have disappeared into thin air.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Even if anyone is caught here or overseas, there is very little hope for the victim to see his life savings again.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Would it not be possible for the Ministry to mandate the banks to offer more protection for the elderly and vulnerable from falling victim to such scams?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Would it not make sense for the gatekeeper of the conduit for interbank transfer to play a bigger role in combating such crimes?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: One of my residents was tricked into giving out his OTP in a similar tech support scam and ended up losing his life savings in two local banks.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The scammer did his homework and contacted the resident late on a Friday night.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: By the time this resident realised that something was not right, the bank had closed and he could only call the after-office helpline for assistance.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The perplexing part of this case is that only one bank would stop the illegal transfer while the other could not, and both financial institutions are using the same international remittance network.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Another one of my residents was so spooked by such scams that he asked the bank to issue him an ordinary bank card with no wireless payment feature or linked to any international debit or credit service provider.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: He was told there is no such card anymore, but he could request the bank to limit the transaction amount or disable the debit feature.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: If such features can be disabled with a phone call, what safeguards are there to prevent scammers from reversing it?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: This is exactly what the elderly resident was worried about.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: He just wanted a simple bank card for cash withdrawal.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: This educated resident told me he needs to be careful because he knows his reflexes, cognition, memory and everything else he took for granted in the past are ageing, too.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: While the scammer may work on this victim for hours, the success of such scams hinges on the split-second transfer of money out of the victim's bank account.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: If we have a cooling-off period for direct sale, can the banks offer such feature for interbank transfer on demand as well?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Any change of mind for such a cooling-off service will require a visit to the bank in person.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Although this sounds like a low-tech approach, you can certainly buy some time, and time is what scammers do not want.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I am not asking the authorities to slow everything down.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I am only asking the authorities to get the banks to provide an option for the elderly and vulnerable to protect their life savings.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The Police can only do so much to investigate after the crime has been committed.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: It does not have the weapon of choice to stop or slow down the scammer from laying hands on the ill-gotten gains.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: It was reported in the news yesterday that the number of banking scam calls or messages went up sharply in January this year with 105 cases reported, compared to 38 cases in the previous three months combined.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: To me, that is a red flag for the authorities to take the lead to fight scammers that capitalise on the banking system to steal from the elderly and vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Online scams and crimes are, indeed, on the rise, Sir.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I agree with the Member that each case is very painful, very sad.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The few cases that Mr Png Eng Huat mentioned fall into the latter category.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The criminals can reach out to their victims either through phone calls, messages, emails, even cyberattacks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the Singapore Police Force (SPF), the National Crime Prevention Council (NCPC) and our banks, have been working together to protect Singaporeans against these online scams and crimes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our efforts have focused on the following four areas.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Public agencies have stepped up educational initiatives through media campaigns, roadshows and community outreach programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MoneySENSE, our national financial education programme, regularly puts out public messages to caution the public against online crimes and scams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Banks also regularly remind their customers, "Do not disclose your account details, user IDs, passwords or SMS One-time passwords (OTPs) to anyone, no matter who they claim to be".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Bank customers have also been encouraged to maintain strong cyber hygiene by installing anti-virus software and regularly updating it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, MAS has issued various regulations and guidelines related to the security of online transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fraud monitoring and detection systems are another prerequisite to facilitate timely detection and blocking of suspicious transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On a real-time basis, transaction alerts are sent to customers to allow them to quickly notify their banks of any unauthorised payment transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These security measures to curb unauthorised transactions have become industry norms in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Where specific bank accounts have been identified to be associated with scams, the SPF's Anti-Scam Centre will freeze the relevant bank accounts as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Doing so disrupts the scam operation and increases the chances of recovering victims' monies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In this regard, Mr Png Eng Huat suggested a possible cooling-off option and feature for elderly customers to opt-in, so that when they make a transfer, maybe it will happen 24 hours later.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is something that we can discuss with the banks as a possible way to help, as an option for elderly customers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fourth, where the scam is cross-border in nature, SPF will seek the cooperation of their foreign counterparts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Transnational Commercial Crime Task Force (TCTF) was set up in October 2017 to investigate transnational scams, such as China Officials Impersonation Scams, Internet Love Scams and Credit-for-Sex scams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It actively shares information with foreign law enforcement agencies and, where possible, works with them to mount joint operations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But as Mr Png Eng Huat mentioned, the sophistication of scams will continue to evolve.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The cross-border nature also poses additional challenges and limits what our public agencies and banks can achieve on their own.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why core to our anti-cyber scam strategy has to be public awareness and education, so that all of us remain vigilant and do not fall prey to cybercrimes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: During this COVID-19, we are all constantly reminded to, first, wash our hands frequently; second, do not touch our faces unnecessarily; and third, when we are unwell, go see a doctor and do not go to school or do not go to work.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These are the three key pieces of advice that we should heed.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Likewise, the three key pieces of advice to fight cyber scams are: one, never draw money from our account to pass to anyone, even if they claim to be from the authorities; two, never share your personal and banking details, especially your OTP with anyone; and, if in doubt, three, consult your loved ones, call the anti-scam helpline or visit NCPC's Scam Alert website at scamalert.sg.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As the Police advise – "Don't Panic, Don't Believe, Don't Give", "别慌。别信。别给。" The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) will elaborate about its strategies to address scams at its COS debate.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Just as SkillsFuture is crucial for the private sector, it is also vital for the public sector to embrace SkillsFuture.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This is especially so today, with technology and digitalisation disrupting work, workers and workplaces regardless of where you are in the world and what you do.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Today, we have seen several traditional jobs being automated completely, for example, services that are now online and where customers can do self-checkout and self-help.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: On the other hand, we also see some jobs that are performed very differently today, for instance, through deploying Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and "training" robots, as opposed to performing the manual tasks ourselves.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: What this means for Singapore is that as a small and open economy, we need to be able to transform and innovate new products and services to maintain our competitiveness while working within manpower constraints.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Technology and longer career spans are two positive opportunities that can help us overcome our constraints.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This underscores the importance of Industry 4.0 and SkillsFuture to ensure that the public sector stays ready, relevant and resilient.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: To achieve a win-win-win outcome for workers, employers and the economy, we must continually upskill our workers to equip them with in-demand skills of today and of the future.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This will help them take on quality jobs and better jobs should their jobs become automated or replaced by machines.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In this vein, how does the public sector intend to help its officers achieve lifelong employability, given that the skill requirements and jobs would evolve throughout a longer career span?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: How has it been engaging the Labour Movement to help officers understand, embrace and thrive in a new environment that is increasingly dynamic and even disruptive?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: What has been the progress in terms of skills upgrading within the Public Service?

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: There are several reasons why these lapses have occurred: first, outsourcing of work, with price as the greatest determining factor of selecting contracts.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: Second, lack of expertise, especially among mid- to high-level bureaucrats.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: Third, high frequency of staff rotation and poor protocols in relation to the handing over of duties.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: Fourth, insufficient use of technology to reduce human error.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: Fifth, a lack of accreditation or standards for public officers.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: Our public officers also need to possess the relevant expertise in order to carry out their responsibilities and plan, staff and supervise projects closely.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: This is so that we can ensure that our public officers can work closely with stakeholders in the various industries to ensure quality delivery of public services, public projects and smooth completion of private sector projects.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: It is, therefore, imperative that our Public Service pushes itself to continually improve and keep up with the times.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: Can the Government also consider giving out scholarships to nurture and attract talent in these fields?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the latest Estimates, this has risen to $1.05 billion.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PMO houses functions that cut across Ministries relating to climate and population, for example.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But over the years, PMO has also come to acquire coordinating and leadership roles in a number of areas where there would seem to be a more natural fit with domain Ministries.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, why is National Research Foundation (NRF) programme under PMO rather than MTI since research should be pursued in such a way as to maximise and multiply its benefits to industry and to the economy, which is MTI's purview?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A similar point could be made for the National Security and Intelligence Coordination programme vis-a-vis the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) which would seem the natural location for the ownership of Total Defence programmes, and the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office (SNDGO) vis-a-vis the Ministry of Communications and Information.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the debate on the GovTech Bill in 2016, I asked why the Cyber Security Agency (CSA) was at that time located in PMO rather than within MINDEF, the answer was, "this is to give CSA the ability to oversee cybersecurity at the national level, and so on".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does this mean that all policymaking fields that function at the national as opposed to sectoral level and cut across Ministries to some degree will eventually come under PMO?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And if so, how do we ensure that the duplication of functions and expertise is minimised vis-a-vis domain Ministries, which generally have more staff with expertise in the domains?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How would we also ensure that due weight in policymaking is given to subject matter experts in the domain Ministries?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Worldwide, technology is disrupting business models, reshaping supply chains and creating new jobs.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: In this creative disruption process, those who cannot keep up will be left behind.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Given this context, I would like to ask the Minister, over the years, how has our Public Service reinvented itself to keep up with competition?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: How has the Public Service embraced technology to render itself more efficient and to serve its clients more effectively?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: What has the Public Service done to encourage, induce and catalyse large-scale innovations among businesses and society at large?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: According to a Zaobao report, Mr Lan Shaomin, the current Party Secretary of Suzhou, when he was the Mayor of Taizhou in 2016, gave out "Snail Awards" (蜗牛奖) to 57 individuals and organisations for their "slow work" or "non work".

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Does the Public Service, perhaps, in a different but no less urgent way, reward its internal innovators and change agents and punish the procrastinators and non-performers?

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Mr Chairman, my cut today is to discuss how our Public Service can show greater care and empathy in designing and delivering services to citizens.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: In the past few years, the Public Service has embarked on digitalisation to transform the way it delivers services.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: This was elaborated by Minister Vivian Balakrishnan and Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: However, there is still a group of citizens who may be unable to transact digitally, such as some elderly who may be unfamiliar with computers and smart phones or others from low-income families who cannot afford such smart phones or broadband access.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: It is great that the Government seeks higher effectiveness and efficiency of service delivery.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: They could be relatives, college students, grassroots members, corporate employees on corporate social responsibility (CSR) or just helpful neighbours.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Beyond guiding those who are not digitally savvy in society to cope with our nation’s digitalisation journey, such buddy interactions would also promote community bonding and forge a more cohesive society, one where no one is left behind.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: As for hardware, smartphones or laptops and broadband access at home may be taken for granted by many.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: I am also particularly concerned with school children from lower-income families who may not be able to afford a computer or broadband access at home.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: In today’s learning environment, a computer and broadband access are like the "paper and pen" of the past and, therefore, no child should be denied that.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Businesses around the world have increasingly been using digital technologies to upscale their operations, seek better efficiencies and create value for their entities.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There are now countless mobile phone apps and online platforms where businesses can use to acquire, engage and transact with their customers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This has brought about better conveniences, accessibility, outreach and also, importantly, lower transaction fees to their customers due to efficiency gains.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The cost savings from better efficiency and outreach benefited both the businesses and customers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Can I ask if the Public Service would do likewise to tap on digital technology in a bigger way to transform service delivery to citizens and businesses?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Public Service is not starting from ground zero.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It has launched the MOL app for birth registration a couple of years ago and it has just been announced that there will be an enhanced version.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Such service apps can help eliminate the unnecessary inconveniences where businesses or citizens need to go to more than one agency to get things done.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If properly designed, it can also avoid duplication in resources or situations where different sets of officers are serving the same customer in different agencies.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Public Service should look towards integrating its services and, where possible, establish a one-stop user-friendly digital platform, which can also reduce the need for manual delivery of services.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I will deliver my reply in half the time that I was supposed to.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, a strong, competent and forward-looking Public Service has been central to Singapore's success.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It has been so and it will continue to be so.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, if it deals with strategic issues with long-term consequences.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, if it requires close coordination across many agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Third, if it is a nascent new capability where we need to incubate that capability development before we pass it on to a relevant Ministry.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Over time, those agencies that fall under PMO would have satisfied one or more of these criteria.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When the capabilities mature, they will be passed on to the relevant Ministries that best house them.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I would just like to organise them into two sets of answers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, what can the public expect from our Public Service?

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, what can the Public Service officers expect, going forward?

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, as mentioned, digital is a tremendous opportunity for the Public Service to embrace to better deliver our services in a more integrated fashion, at a faster speed, at a lower cost.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And we have heard many examples of this with the MOL app and also the GoBusiness app and I will not repeat what Minister Vivian Balakrishnan and Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary have mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second thing that we can expect with this mindset shift would be the cross-training of our officers to deliver services in an integrated manner.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Various public agencies have come together to, first, co-locate and provide convenience to residents seeking services across different agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is the direction that the Public Service will continue to go in order to deliver quality services to the residents who need help.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, someone who needs help, from financial assistance to housing to employment, can approach the same officer with the same understanding so that he does not need to repeat the story over and over again.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, this is the second example of how the mindset shift has gone on in the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The third shift that we can expect from the Public Service is this.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Public Service is no longer just an agency trying to prevent things from going wrong or bad things from happening.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Now, this is a very different mindset shift.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When we work with a startup, it is not about the startup trying to fit into the current regulations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, the public can certainly expect a more integrated and more efficient Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But what I want to end off on this part is what Mr Cedric Foo mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: No matter how technology-dependent we will be, we will never forget that at the core of the Public Service is the heart for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The way we design the services, the way we design the app, be it for the young or the old, is to make sure that the service is delivered with the heart.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For people who need the service but are unable to access technology, we will make sure that the processes are simplified, the service delivery is integrated, so that they will never be left out.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And that is how we want to design an inclusive Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second part of my speech will, therefore, touch on what the Public Service officers can expect.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: With the changes in public expectations, with the change in job scopes, we will certainly need to change the skillsets of our Public Service officers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I have mentioned this on various occasions and the Prime Minister has also mentioned this during the inaugural Annual Public Service Leadership Dinner in the earlier part of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, we expect Public Service officers not just to be savvy in policymaking, but we also expect them to be good in translating policies into operations, have the ability to communicate and mobilise the public to come and work together to deliver results.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And we want our public officers to have a sense of what is going on beyond Singapore, beyond the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These are the new skillsets that we expect all Public Service leaders to have and this will be how we form leadership teams within the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: One of the things that we will also change is to more regularly rotate Public Service officers across different domains and even within the same domain.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Across different domains, I have mentioned, in that four domain areas – policymaking, operations, communications and mobilisations and international or beyond Public Service exposure.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second thing that we want to do is to make sure that they have the ability to rotate more even within the same domain and this will address one of the points that Dr Teo Ho Pin mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: How do we make sure that we check our own blind spots even if we are doing the same job?

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, in regulatory matters, by being able to go to different agencies and see how different regulatory ideas are applied, will allow our public officers to be much more responsive, much more agile.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The third thing that we can expect our public officers to do is this.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And this will require us to structure their training such that every few years, there will be a booster jab in their skills.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When we ask our Public Service officers to be agile, it cannot be at the age of 40s or 50s.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It must be done systematically, from age 20 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But at the same time, to also bring back good ideas that the public sector may not yet have that are now in the private sector or the people sector or, for that matter, also even in the international organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Having dealt with all the changes that we can expect from the Public Service, I must reiterate one point.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: While the methods can change, the technology can change, the values of the Public Service will not change.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The values of service excellence and integrity will never change in the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Service beyond self, the interests of the country and our people must always come before the interests of the individual officers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The pursuit of excellence is not just for today but always being able to anticipate the challenges of tomorrow, put in place systems and processes before the challenges even arise.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Integrity to do what is right for this generation and for the next.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Just as Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat says, our definition of success is not just how well we deliver for this generation but also for the next.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Integrity also to know that there is no such thing that we are at our best.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: That is, only that we will continue to improve to bring about a better of life for Singaporeans and for a better Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, we will keep engaging the ground, keep improving our processes, keep improving the skillsets of our Public Service officers, in order for us to deliver on a better Singapore, a stronger Singapore and a better future for all of us.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I understand that we are reviewing it but I am just wondering if we can also review and look into what other countries are doing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: There is a long list of countries that are providing the childcare sick leave – I would not read the whole thing – there is Australia, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Israel, Italy, Japan, New Zealand, Norway, Russia, South Africa, Switzerland.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In the interest of time, I would not read them all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But I am just wondering whether PMO can study what other countries are doing, see how successful it is, see how they implement it and then we can do a proper review.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think the Minister once said that all good things will be considered.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This is a good thing that should be considered.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do actually study and we study them holistically, too.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Marriage and Parenthood Support measures, they do work in concert with one another and they have to work within the context of each country.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we will look at all good suggestions in the context of what our young people want.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: If I understood Minister Chan correctly, he said that there are three considerations for determining the functions within PMO.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And I think the third point was that functions are sometimes incubated and then transferred to a Ministry where there is a more natural fit with the domain of that Ministry after a certain period of time.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I think that has been there for quite sometime vis-a-vis MTI.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The NRF also conducts research in many other things, for example, ageing and societal forces as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, there is a good reason why NRF resides under PMO.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, NRF works very closely with MTI and, of course, the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) which is under MTI for the economic portions of it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, whether it is the future of decarbonisation, the future of our bio-medical industries, they work very closely.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have also a very simple way to make sure that this is coordinated closely between NRF, A*STAR and MTI because the Chairperson of A*STAR is also the Permanent Secretary for NRF.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If the two organisations have any issues, then it is actually internalised within the leadership team.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Chairman, I have two questions and one clarification.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The two questions are for Minister Josephine Teo.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The first was the number of PRs that do not transition to citizenship.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think there was some very helpful data that was released in the Population in Brief document from September last year that tells you at what age group these PRs are at.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But what about those who do not transit to citizenship?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second clarification pertains to the question I had on integration.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think the Minister also restated the point that new immigrants have to play their part and get involved.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But on the flip side, we have two or three decades now of immigration experience.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: What are some of the points that the immigrants themselves raised?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: What are the issues that they had in integrating with the community?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The third point is a clarification for Minister Vivian Balakrishnan.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think Minister Vivian Balakrishnan said that Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary was going to say something about smart lamp posts but I do not believe the Senior Minister of State said anything about that.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think they were running out of time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It has been about half a million; we have basically kept it at that level.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There will always be a certain number that may take a while before they decide to become citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If they leave Singapore and do not return for a long period of time, then their re-entry permits could be cancelled.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As they become citizens, the length of time they take to become citizens does not matter.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some take a shorter time; some take a longer time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Sometimes, it is a matter of thinking about it themselves, because it is hard to eventually make that transition.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think the important thing is that we have kept the PR population stable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Then, to the Member's other question, I think this is with regard to integration as to what do the new citizens themselves say about the challenges of integration.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The practical thing will be that social habits are different.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Singapore has high density living, and most will live in public housing, very close to their neighbours.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is why a lot of the emphasis on integration is carried out through the People's Association, which has the ability to reach to a large number of citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This includes new as well as long-time citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is almost certainly that second generation citizens acquire the features of local life very quickly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And it is through the second generation that they themselves become naturalised.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think this is not unique to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope collectively, we have addressed the Member's concern about data security and privacy, and the need to get that balance right in order to maintain public confidence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Senior Minister State Janil Puthucheary may not have mentioned lamp posts specifically, but he did talk about security.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I think this House is also aware of the overarching policy and legislative framework for data security, both within Government and in the private sector.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: Historically, many Government agencies and Ministries design systems and processes from their points of view.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: I think the public will be well-served if Government agencies can think "the other way around" and try to design processes from the citizens' or businesses' points of view.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, indeed, we totally agree with what Mr Cedric had said.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have asked people, "If you are a parent-to-be, what are the questions that you would want answered?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: What are the services that you would want?" We do what we call a Service Journey.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And from there on, all their services will be designed around making it more convenient for the people that they are serving.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is how we have been able to achieve breakthroughs in the MOL app and even Our Tampines Hub.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: How we lay out the services to welcome the residents whom we serve, how we design the processes that they have to go through.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: How our officers speak to the residents is also an acquired skill.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In order to do that, we make sure that our Public Service leaders walk-the-talk.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We make sure people, right from the leadership level, take the lead, by going onto the ground to serve the residents.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we have many examples of this whereby even Chief Executives and the leadership team will be at the service counter serving the residents, seeing how the residents respond to the policies from different agencies, what are the challenges and how we can redesign the processes to do better.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have senior officers, for example, in the communications department and various other public officers walking the ground on weekends, talking to ordinary Singaporeans, hearing their feedback first-hand, unfiltered.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is part of the work that the feedback unit Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home (REACH) officers are doing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But it is not just the REACH officers that are doing this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Actually, many of our officers whom I am very proud of volunteered to do this so that they can go to the ground and hear for themselves first-hand how people are responding and reacting to the changes that they make.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, it is design upfront, change in their mindset and training of the officers in order to deliver a much more empathetic Public Service.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Sorry, Mr Chair, can I just give an example to Mr Leon Perera?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I talked about incubation and then, subsequently, we transfer it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MSO started in PMO; now, it has gone on to MND when the capabilities have been matured.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Seah, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

text: Mr Chairman, on behalf of all Members who spoke, I wish to thank Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean, Ministers Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, Mrs Josephine Teo, Mr Ong Ye Kung and Mr Chan Chun Sing, and Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary, for their comprehensive and assuring responses on matters ranging from climate change, population challenges, Smart Nation initiatives and the Public Service.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

text: I propose to take the break now and I will take the Chair at 4.40 pm.
